title: Personal Physician
need: I'd like a doctor who already knows me
summary: An annual membership with one named physician: appointments within a working day, a full hour when you need it, and a direct line that isn't a call centre.
intro: Most of medicine is ordinary: a cough that lingers, a result that needs explaining, a prescription, a worry that is probably nothing. What makes it go well is a doctor who already knows your history. Membership gives you one, alongside a small team who cover when they are away and who read the same notes.
image_alt: A man in his sixties mid-sentence, describing something, lit by a tall window
for_whom: People who want continuity rather than a different doctor each visit
Families who would like one practice to hold everyone's records
Anyone managing a long-term condition who wants it overseen, not just repeated

includes.title: A named physician
includes.detail: Chosen with you after your first appointment. They lead your care, and specialists report back to them.

includes.title: Appointments within one working day
includes.detail: Thirty minutes as standard; sixty when the problem needs it. In person or by video.

includes.title: A direct line
includes.detail: Your coordinator's number and email. Messages are answered the same working day.

includes.title: Prescriptions and referrals
includes.detail: Issued promptly, with a letter that explains the reasoning, not just a form.

includes.title: An annual review
includes.detail: A structured hour each year to look back and plan ahead, with bloods taken beforehand.

process.detail: Your history, medications, family background, and what you want from a physician.
With your consent we request your records, so nothing starts from scratch. You keep your NHS GP.
See your physician or, when they are away, a colleague who has read your notes first.

fees.note: Appointments included. Tests and medicines are quoted before they are arranged.
Two adults and their children under 18.
30 minutes, in person or by video.

faqs.q: Do I still need an NHS GP?
faqs.a: We recommend keeping one. With your permission we copy letters to your NHS GP so both records stay complete, and some long-term prescriptions are simpler to continue there.
Usually not. Most private medical insurance covers specialist and diagnostic care after a referral, not primary care. We'll tell you plainly what is likely to be covered before you commit.

faqs.q: What happens when my physician is away?
faqs.a: Each physician's list is covered by one of two named colleagues. They read your notes before seeing you, and your physician picks up where they left off.
